newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on exports, soy and Canada.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on exports, soy and Canada.

text.p: Reminders of stiff export competition, a downward correction in the soy complex and confirmation Canada was railing wheat to be shipped through a U.S. port pressured CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
The Canadian Wheat Board said Wednesday it is shipping an "average sized" cargo load of wheat to Portland.
Also a Philippine firm Wednesday rejected bids for 40,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, Manila traders said, and there was news Japan agreed to buy 900,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia in calendar 1997.
Egypt's main commodities buyer said the 400,000 tonnes of Australian wheat Egypt bought about a month ago from the Australian Wheat Board would be shipped in April and May.
Traders also said there were prospects for heavy deliveries Friday against the March contract.

There were nearly 2.5 million bushels of wheat registered in Toledo for possible delivery and the market was expecting nearly all of the wheat to be delivered. Friday is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT March contracts.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 6-1/4 at $3.70-3/4.
Pressure on the market also came from improved soil moisture levels over the past week in key U.S. wheat states.

Wheat was underpinned by fund buying estimated at roughly 10 million bushels. Goldenberg Hehmeyer and LIT America each bought 2.5 million bushels of May and Dean Witter bought one million bushels of July, traders said.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold 1.3 million bushels of July and Smith Barney bought 1.5 million July and sold one million July, traders said.
Technicians early Wednesday reported the four and 20-day moving averages as bullish.
First support in the March was at $3.70-1/2 and second support was at $3.60-1/2. The session low for March was $3.70-1/2.
First resistance for March was $3.80-1/2 and second resistance was $3.90-1/2. The session high for March was $3.78.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed at 55 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 23,775 traded Tuesday.
Cargill Investor Services bought 200 May $3.30 puts at 1-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 200 May $3.50 puts and sold 200 May $3.70 puts at four to 11-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 5,653 traded Tuesday.
